newsitem.title: USA: Mo. AG asks court to clarify health funding ruling.
newsitem.headline: Mo. AG asks court to clarify health funding ruling.

text.p: Missouri Attorney General Jay Nixon on Friday asked a federal judge to clarify whether his decision overturning a ban on state funding to Planned Parenthood in 1996 would apply to a prohibition approved this year as well.

Gov. Mel Carnahan signed a state budget Thursday that included a health services package eliminating state funding to Planned Parenthood. Carnahan, who opposed the legislative action, also asked Nixon to seek a court clarification.
"It is defendants' desire to comply with this court's permanent injunction and to follow the law," the attorney general's motion filed with the U.S. District Court in Kansas City stated.

Judge Fernando Gaitan Jr ruled in June 1996 there was "no rational basis for the distinction between Planned Parenthood and the other eligible recipients for the state appropriated family-planning funds."

Gaitan then entered a preliminary and permanent injunction against the state ban on funding to Planned Parenthood, which at the time allowed abortions to be performed at two of its nine Missouri clinics.
In requesting a clarification, Nixon argued that Gaitan retained jurisdiction over enforcement or modification of injunctions. No court date has been set in the matter.
